policy.why: CI proves what CI can reach. These are the device classes it cannot: they are physical machines in a lab, and nothing watches how long it has been since one of them last ran the gates. The Windows suite went nineteen days and eight failures before anybody noticed. A class belongs here only if a hosted runner cannot verify it; everything else belongs in .github/workflows/ci.yml.
policy.gate: scripts/check-release.py refuses a tag while any class here is STALE, FAILING or NEVER, the same way it refuses a README and site that link different Hugging Face repositories.
policy.recording: Rows are written by scripts/device-evidence.py --record from the runner's own --caps output on the machine in question, and the class's `expect` block refuses a recording made on the wrong one. A row is a machine's statement about a machine, not a line somebody typed.
